items: Emission sources: burning wood and fossil fuels raises local pollution; factories and power plants release SOx and NOx, vehicles release CO, PM and VOCs.

Meteorological conditions: wind, temperature and humidity affect the dispersion and concentration of pollutants; a layer of warm air trapping pollutants near the ground (an inversion) can cause poor air quality.
Natural events: wildfires release large amounts of smoke and PM; dust storms can lower air quality significantly.
Seasonal changes: heating or cooling of buildings in different seasons increases emissions, and seasonal pollen adds to poor air quality.

blocks.prompt: Which natural factor can improve air quality, and describe the factors that affect it (MCQ IV; exercise Q.6)?
blocks.explanation: Rainfall improves air quality by washing particles and soluble gases out of the air. Air quality depends on emission sources (fuel burning, industry, traffic), meteorology (wind disperses, calm air and temperature inversions trap pollutants), natural events (wildfires, dust storms) and the seasons (heating and cooling demand, pollen).

items: Factors: emission sources; meteorology (wind, temperature, humidity, inversions); natural events (wildfires, dust storms); seasonal changes (heating, cooling, pollen).
